decisions.reason: Attributes the sole crash to plugin A's unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call in SessionProgressBar, grounded in the console excerpt and the source excerpt; explains alpha.2 dropped the prop in favor of useSessionStatus while useSessions stays. Correctly states plugin B uses no standard-kit hooks and throws nothing; does not claim useSessions was removed.

Explains via the render-tree note that the dock is one list slot whose entries mount under one shared DrawerErrorBoundary, so A's throw unmounts the whole boundary subtree including B's chips; cites the unmounted-entries console line. Notes the attach button survives because conversation.input.left is a separate slot under its own boundary.

Reads the disable-A experiment as proving render-crash coupling (B was never broken) while explicitly noting it does not prove B is fully alpha.2-compatible nor that the A crash is the only dock defect. Explains reinstalling B could never help and refutes the colleague's both-plugins-removed theory using B's hook-free render path and the single console error.

Proposed code reads pending through useSessionStatus(...).pendingInteraction on alpha.2 with a legacy-hook fallback, capability-detected calls and stable empty fallbacks so at worst only pending indicators hide while running/todos/token/ETA keep working. Explains silent degradation: a throwing tenant re-unmounts co-tenants via the shared boundary, so a missing indicator is cosmetic versus a multi-plugin outage.

Verification uses hard refresh without host restart (client bundles re-fetch), asserts both entries render together with zero errors and no boundary-fallback line, and covers B's paste/remove/re-paste regression with A enabled. Hygiene: tenants capability-detect hooks and may wrap their own entry in a local boundary; host could mount per-entry boundaries with the trade-off in boundary count, layout holes, and reset cost spelled out.

caps.reason: The final remedy fixes plugin A's component and optionally the host's boundary granularity; the report explicitly rejects reinstalling or fixing B and denies the two symptoms are independent plugin-level bugs.
